```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r}
library(tidymarkers)
```

The package is not tied to Arabidopsis: any FASTA and VCF will do. The heavy steps
(reading files, design) are shown here as code and are not run when the document
is built.

## Arbitrary genome

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Rsamtools index (.fai is created once) - read only the needed chromosomes
genome <- read_genome_fasta("my_assembly.fa", seqids = c("chr1", "chr2"))

# or map "raw" names to convenient ones
read_genome_fasta("my_assembly.fa",
                  chrom_map = c("1" = "chr1", "2" = "chr2"))
```

## Your own VCF

`read_variants_vcf()` reads in a streaming fashion (`vroom`), supports `.vcf.gz` and
expands multiallelic ALT into rows; IUPAC codes are collapsed to `N`, symbolic
alleles (`<DEL>`, `*`, `.`) are dropped.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
variants <- read_variants_vcf("my.vcf.gz", chrom = "chr1",
                              start = 100000, end = 200000)
head(variants)                       # chrom, pos, ref, alt (rows)
```

## Target site, masking and design

Your own variant is given as a `chrom/pos/ref/alt` table (SNP, MNP and InDel - rows):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
snp <- tibble::tibble(chrom = "chr1", pos = 150001L, ref = "G", alt = "A")

# mask other variants under the primer so they are not carried into the oligo
genome[["chr1"]] <- mask_positions(genome[["chr1"]], variants$pos - 1L)

assay <- assemble_kasp_assay(genome, snp, variants = variants,
                             max_footprint_variants = 0)   # N-masking as a limit
assay
```

## Batch

```{r, eval = FALSE}
loci <- variants[order(variants$pos), ][1:200, c("chrom", "pos", "ref", "alt")]
design_kasp_markers(genome, loci, BPPARAM = BiocParallel::MulticoreParam(4))
```

See also `vignettes/kasp-intro.Rmd` and `?read_variants_vcf`, `?assemble_kasp_assay`.
